what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection in adults and children who are at least 3 years old or weigh at least 35 pounds (about 17 kg). It works by attacking the hepatitis C virus directly, helping to clear the virus from your body. Many patients are cured after completing treatment.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or split it. If you have trouble swallowing tablets, talk to your pharmacist or doctor. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. For children who cannot swallow tablets, a pellet form (in granules) is available — sprinkle the granules onto one or more spoonfuls of non-acidic soft food such as pudding or chocolate syrup and swallow right away without chewing.
dosing: The most common adult dose is one tablet (90 mg ledipasvir / 400 mg sofosbuvir) taken once a day. The length of treatment is usually 8, 12, or 24 weeks depending on your specific type of hepatitis C, your liver health, and whether you have been treated before. Your doctor will decide the right dose and duration for you. Do not stop taking this medicine early without talking to your doctor, even if you feel better.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 18 hours since your scheduled time, take it as soon as you remember. If it has been more than 18 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Never take two doses at the same time or double up to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep it away from moisture, heat, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids (like Maalox or Mylanta) within 4 hours before or after your dose, as they can reduce how well this medicine works. Do not take proton pump inhibitors (like omeprazole or Prilosec) in higher-than-standard doses without your doctor's approval. Avoid herbal supplements, especially St. John's Wort, as it can make this medicine less effective and may cause treatment failure. Do not drink large amounts of alcohol, as it can harm your liver. Tell all your doctors and pharmacists about every medicine, vitamin, and supplement you take, because many drugs can interact with this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: extreme tiredness or weakness, unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, stomach pain, nausea or vomiting, feeling cold especially in your arms or legs, dizziness, or fast or irregular heartbeat — these could be signs of a rare but serious side effect called lactic acidosis. Also call your doctor if you notice yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or signs of liver problems. If you take amiodarone (a heart rhythm medicine), tell your doctor immediately before starting this medication, as a dangerous drop in heart rate can occur. Contact your doctor if your hepatitis B infection gets worse or comes back while on treatment.
when_it_works: Most people do not feel any different while taking this medicine, but it is working inside your body. Your doctor will check your blood periodically during and after treatment to see if the virus is responding. Treatment success is measured 12 weeks after you finish your full course — this is called a 'sustained virologic response' (SVR), which means the virus is no longer detected in your blood and is considered a cure for hepatitis C. Do not stop taking this medicine just because you feel well — finishing the full course is very important.
special_populations: Pregnancy: There is limited safety data for use during pregnancy. Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor before breastfeeding. Kidney disease: Use with caution in patients with severe kidney disease or those on dialysis — your doctor will monitor you closely. Liver disease (cirrhosis): This medicine can be used in patients with mild to moderate cirrhosis, but patients with severe or decompensated cirrhosis may need additional medicines and closer monitoring. Elderly patients (65 and older): No dose adjustment is needed, but your doctor may monitor you more carefully. Children: A pellet/granule form is available for children who weigh at least 17 kg (about 35 lbs) and who cannot swallow tablets.
